CRITICAL BUG FOUND & FIXED: backend startup crashed with TypeError after first POST /admin/meta/secrets because platform_settings.secrets._meta (dict) got iterated as os.environ[k]=v — patched server.py to skip non-string values.

critical.issue: server.py startup crashed (TypeError: str expected, not dict) because it iterated ALL keys of platform_settings.secrets (including sub-dict _meta added by /admin/meta/secrets) into os.environ. After ANY secrets update, the next backend restart would fail lifespan and take the whole API down. Fixed by adding isinstance(v, str) guard.

critical_code_review_comments: admin_routes.get_current_admin correctly enforces type=='admin' — good isolation between admin/app JWTs (verified by cross-cookie tests).

admin_routes.impersonate mints an app access_token with type='access' — combined with security.get_current_user bearer-first ordering (auth[7:] before cookies) this gives clean impersonation without shared password. Test confirmed Bearer takes priority over cookie.
security.get_current_user checks office status in ('suspended','canceled') → 403. This blocks /auth/me and every other tenant endpoint. Verified suspend/reactivate cycle works.

admin_routes.update_secrets: values are correctly never returned in any endpoint (test_write_only confirms fake_xxxxxx string NEVER appears in /admin/meta/status body). However the current data shape (secrets._meta as sub-dict) is what triggered the startup crash — see critical issue above. Recommend flattening.

core_routes.create_process overage: count uses count_documents({'office_id': ...}) before insert; there's a small TOCTOU window under concurrency (two parallel POSTs could both pass the hard-limit check and each insert one). Not exploitable in normal use but acknowledge for future.

admin_routes.pay_charge OVERWRITES valor_final with paid amount — this is intentional for partial-payment recording but note that if valor_final was set at creation (data.valor - desconto), it's now lost. Report the received amount in receipts, keep valor_final untouched for accounting integrity — consider storing valor_recebido separately.

admin_routes.list_offices does N+1 queries per office (users count, procs count, socio find, whatsapp find, last_msg find). With 25+ offices this is 100+ DB calls per page load. Acceptable now but plan aggregation pipeline for scale.
admin_routes.admin_dashboard also does per-office queries in loops for atencao — same N+1 pattern. Consider a single $lookup aggregation.

rca of the issue: STARTUP CRASH RCA — POST /admin/meta/secrets writes both raw values (secrets.META_TEST_TOKEN='fake…') AND metadata under secrets._meta (as a nested dict with keys like META_TEST_TOKEN_at, META_TEST_TOKEN_status). On next backend startup, server.py iterated `for k, v in (doc.get('secrets') or {}).items()` and hit `os.environ[k] = v` where v = {'META_TEST_TOKEN_at': '...', 'META_TEST_TOKEN_status': 'invalid'} — dict is not str → TypeError → Lifespan failed → 'Application startup failed. Exiting.' → uvicorn crash → every subsequent request times out. Reproduction: (1) POST /admin/meta/secrets with meta_test_token=anything, (2) supervisorctl restart backend, (3) any API call → gateway timeout. MITIGATION APPLIED: added `isinstance(v, str)` guard in server.py startup loop. LONG-TERM: refactor admin_routes.update_secrets to store metadata under a sibling field (platform_settings.secrets_meta) rather than nested under platform_settings.secrets.
